description:
Exact arbitrary-grid rank checks and symbolic monotone-family boundaries.

Reuses the frozen sharp-cost rational arithmetic. Populations in analytical
certificates are symbolic counts, never expanded into label tables. Finite
checks support the proof and implementation; they establish neither novelty
nor empirical usefulness. All decimal bounds are rounded outward.

grid_checks.scope: Every nonempty declared grid in the finite range; zero envelope support is excluded from bins, and no targets are added.

protocol.certificate_construction: tau=1/k^3, epsilon=eta=1/k, kappa=k, P=ceil(3*N*k^4/m); no P*m table is allocated
protocol.claim_boundary: Analytical finite checks support proofs and implementation, not novelty, empirical model usefulness, nonzero-table efficiency, or a general monotone-family sharp theorem. Sparse grids use their exact Z_K, not log(N)/e. No CLI limits or supported grid domain are changed.
protocol.counterexample_construction: tau=1/k, beta=1/k^2, H=J=k^3, tail lengths H*2^j for j=0,...,J, plus a uniform baseline; D is a symbolic formula and is never expanded
protocol.status: Fixed after exploratory proof and small-grid checks, before the saved broader calculation; not external preregistration

theorem.budget_family: Every nonempty subset K of {1,...,m}; N=max K
theorem.conclusion: OPT_0 and C_NEG are asymptotic to log(1/delta)*Z_K/tau uniformly in the other parameters
theorem.limit: tau tends to zero and rho=log(1/delta)*N/(P*m*tau) tends to zero
theorem.objective: Expected distinct unit-cost queries on the all-zero fixed-loss table; validity for every fixed table and almost-sure finite zero-table certification

protocol.title: Sharp audit cost for arbitrary budget grids and a monotone-family boundary

rounding.lower: Each bin lower bound rounds down before summation; counterexample ratios round down.
rounding.upper: Linear total cost rounds up; upper decimal bounds round up and lower decimal bounds round down.
